abstract.p: This paper presents the first adaptively simulation secure functional encryption (FE) schemes for attribute-weighted sums. In such an FE scheme, encryption takes as input N pairs of attribute {(xi, zi)} i∈[N ] for some N ∈ N where the attributes {xi} i∈[N ] are public while the attributes {zi} i∈[N ] are private. The indices i ∈ [N ] are referred to as the slots. A secret key corresponds to some weight function f , and decryption recovers the weighted sum N i=1 f (xi)zi. This is an important functionality with a wide range of potential real life applications. In the proposed FE schemes attributes are viewed as vectors and weight functions are arithmetic branching programs (ABP). We present two schemes with varying parameters and levels of adaptive security.
